title: Sunday parades, Captain Darcy and the drill rank women
summary: Parades were big on Sundays; a captain hired Willie, and he played for women's drill ranks that formed letters in the street.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Did they have a parade about every week, every Sunday?

Well, sometimes every Sunday mostly they used to parade, big parade. They used to play for them. You see, like, how do you call it? Like, in May, you know, the second Sunday in May. The odd fellas. Oh, Captain Darcy. You know Captain Darcy?

Well, he wouldn't get no, he looked like a white man. He wouldn't get nobody with Willie. Come to my house two o'clock in the morning. That must be Eddie, I think, huh? He got a sister there across the street, but he lived down on Denver Street somewhere.
He's a bass player, too, isn't he?

No, he didn't play music at all. He just was, he's a Mason. And he would just come high Willie. He went high Willie, he would, for the band. Oh, he'd come get it paid out on, put on the such a bottom one to keep Willie. Yeah. And he used to play for them women, them Bill-ranked women, you know, all when they drill in the street, and they make letters with themselves. Oh, yeah. And they make letters with themselves. I used to play for all them, you know, it must have been good to do that. Had to.
I never saw them make letters in the street. You saw them?
You never saw it? It's something pretty, yeah, they could make the letters.
Some of the ladies in the Elks organization do that sometimes. I mean, they could go and- Yeah, they make letters. March, big march around in circles and different things. Yeah.

Well, the Patriots, my husband used to be with, would play with, and Captain Dawson, and they had them women, the number seven drill rank, and the women. They really made letters with themselves. I don't know how they could do it. They formed the letter. Make letters. I guess they just, they done a practice, they self-ture it. They make them letters. It was something to look at, I'm telling them.
